title: Customer Lighthouse Signal to Roadmap Admission Protocol
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our current intake path conflates volume signals with strategic escalation signals, causing opaque prioritization for top accounts. Goal: Define a deterministic 'Lighthouse' signal taxonomy and an admission protocol that maps customer advocacy events (escalations, exec asks, contract milestones) to a bounded runway and commitment class on the roadmap. This ticket defines the protocol, acceptance criteria, and implementation handoff for PM/AE/CS/Eng flows.
business_rationale: Top 25 accounts drive ~40% of committed ARR for Dedicated & Private customers. A reproducible admission protocol reduces decision latency, minimizes political rework, and aligns delivery SLAs to contractual commitments—improving renewal NPS and preserving engineering prioritization capacity.
success_metrics: 1) Mean time from Lighthouse event -> roadmap admission decision <= 10 business days. 2) % of admitted items with signed SLA/runway <= 95%. 3) Reduction in urgent scope-swaps caused by untracked escalations by 50% within Q4.
acceptance_criteria: Lighthouse taxonomy documented and published in Confluence (signals + weight + TTL)
Admission form (CS/AE) implemented with required fields and attachments in Drive/Notion
Automated intake ticket created in Linear with prefilled metadata and routing rules
Runway class mapping (fast-track / negotiated / roadmap-backlog) codified with clear SLOs
First pilot with three Strategic accounts completed and retrospective published
decision_log: 2025-09-25: Decided to separate Lighthouse signals from volume NPS-based requests; signals must include exec escalation, sales motion milestone, regulatory blocker, and strategic partnership ask
2025-10-01: Agreed on three runway classes (fast-track 2wk SLA, negotiated 4-8wk SLA, roadmap-backlog 1+ release cadence) to avoid open-ended commitments
2025-10-07: PM/CS will own initial triage; Engineering provides feasibility triage within 5 business days for fast-track candidates
tradeoffs: Tight SLAs increase context-switching for infra teams; mitigated by limiting fast-track to 2 active items per ENG squad
Formalizing admission may lengthen initial customer-facing response time; mitigated by committing to a rapid acknowledgement and triage within 48 hours
Automated ticketing requires metadata discipline from CS/AE; we'll build a lightweight form to reduce friction
risks: Over-indexing on Lighthouse signals could starve product-led improvements that emerge from aggregate usage data
Customers may treat admission as a guarantee; improper communication could create SLA disputes
Engineering capacity estimates may drift; need telemetry to detect scope creep early

pilot_plan: Select 3 lighthouse candidates (2 existing renewals, 1 strategic partnership). Run pilot for 6 weeks: week 0 intake + triage, weeks 1-4 engineering delivery (if fast-track), week 5 retrospective and SLA sign-off. Measure MTTR and stakeholder satisfaction.
rollout_plan: 1) Pilot (3 accounts) -> 2) Expand to top-25 accounts for Q4 renewals -> 3) Bake into CS playbooks and SSO/Legal templates. Target org-wide rollout by end of Q1 2026.
